name: Operating Profit
description: Calculate operating profit after cost of goods sold and operating expenses.
business_contexts: a retailer calculating operating profit after COGS and store operating expenses
a manufacturer calculating operating profit after COGS and plant overhead
a software company calculating operating profit after COGS and SG&A
a restaurant chain calculating operating profit after COGS and operating costs
a distributor calculating operating profit after COGS and warehousing expenses
question_patterns: Given the revenue, COGS, and operating expenses below, what is operating profit?
Calculate operating profit from the figures given.
What is operating profit, given the revenue, COGS, and operating expenses shown?
Calculate operating profit by subtracting COGS and operating expenses from revenue given.
Using the figures below, what is operating profit?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate gross profit = revenue − cogs
Step 2: Calculate operating profit = gross profit − operating_expenses
key_insight: Operating profit takes gross profit one step further by netting out the day-to-day cost of running the business — everything except financing and taxes.
common_mistakes: Stopping at gross profit and forgetting to subtract operating expenses
Subtracting operating expenses from revenue directly instead of from gross profit
framework_soundbite: Operating profit is gross profit minus operating expenses — the business's core earning power before financing and tax.
